faqs.question: What is a good first Halloween costume for a newborn?
faqs.answer: Pick something that works lying down and asleep, such as a loose spring-roll swaddle for a single photo or a sleepsuit with stitched felt, like the baby bat or glow-worm. Skip hoods that can slip over the face.

faqs.question: Can my baby sleep in their Halloween costume?
faqs.answer: No. A costume is ordinary clothing, not sleepwear, and the US children's sleepwear flammability standard in 16 CFR 1615 does not cover it. Change the baby into their usual sleepwear for bed and keep costume pieces out of the cot.

faqs.question: How much should I spend on a baby Halloween costume?
faqs.answer: The onesie-based builds in this guide are estimated at US$5–9 each for felt, fabric paint and a beanie. A baby moves through a 0–3 month size in about three months, so a costume that doubles as everyday wear is better value than a one-night plush suit.

faqs.question: What size costume should I buy for my baby's first Halloween?
faqs.answer: Buy for the size the baby will be on 31 October, not the size they are when you shop, and choose one that fits over a single base layer. A costume that is too long becomes a trip hazard once the baby crawls or cruises.

faqs.question: Is face paint safe for babies?
faqs.answer: No. Western Australia's health department advises against painting the face of any child under 3, because paint can get into the eyes or mouth and young skin is sensitive. Draw whiskers or a mask on the beanie instead.

faqs.question: Are pom-poms and buttons on baby costumes a choking hazard?
faqs.answer: They can be. The US small-parts rule in 16 CFR 1501 exempts children's clothing and buttons, so costume trims are not cylinder-tested; tug each one hard and resew or remove anything that moves. Painted or flat-stitched decorations avoid the problem.

faqs.question: How can I tell if my baby is too hot in a costume?
faqs.answer: Feel the tummy or the back of the neck rather than the hands or feet. In a 2020 sling study, babies' skin warmed by up to 1.1°C in 15 minutes while their mothers noticed nothing, so check rather than guess and take a layer off if the skin feels hot or damp.

faqs.question: Can my baby wear a costume in a baby carrier?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the costume replaces a layer rather than adding one. Being carried already warms a baby's skin, so keep them in a single costume sleepsuit and check their tummy after the first 15 minutes.

faqs.question: Is it OK to swaddle my baby for a Halloween costume photo?
faqs.answer: Briefly, if the wrap is loose at the hips and the legs can bend and kick. A 2026 survey of 436 mothers in Riyadh found knowledge of correct swaddling averaged 46.9%, and tight swaddling with straight legs is linked to hip dysplasia.

faqs.question: How do I send my baby's costume photo to the grandparents?
faqs.answer: SubhSandesh's Halloween page has a Family mode that holds up to six photos and a letter, and you get an email the first time they answer. A grandparent without a smartphone will be happier with a printed photo.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Baby Halloween Costume Ideas for Every Stage From 0 to 12 Months

The safest baby Halloween costume ideas follow the baby's stage rather than the costume aisle. A newborn needs something that works lying down, a five-month-old needs a costume that survives tummy time, and a ten-month-old cruising along the sofa needs nothing below the ankle. Built on a plain onesie, most of the 32 costumes below cost an estimated US$5–9 to make, which matters when a 0–3 month size is labelled for just three months of growth.

The photo usually outlives the night. Across all SubhSandesh pages (not Halloween data), phones account for 48.3% of views and the average page draws 11.1 views, so frame the shot in portrait with the baby's face clear. Below: 32 costumes in four stages, a stage-by-stage comparison, and the safety gaps costume labels skip.

## What is a stage-matched baby Halloween costume?

A stage-matched baby costume is designed around what a baby can physically do that month: lie still, sit, crawl or pull up to stand. The risks move as they grow, from the face and neck in the first weeks to the knees and feet by month 10.

Warmth is the constant. A 2025 review by van de Kamp and Daanen notes that babies [cannot remove excess clothing themselves](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12386404), and that adults tend to judge a baby's temperature by their own. Every costume here therefore replaces a layer rather than adding one.

## 32 baby Halloween costume ideas across four developmental stages

Each idea gives the onesie-based build, a safety note and a rough DIY cost. Estimates assume you own a plain sleepsuit and buy only felt, fabric paint or a beanie.

### Newborn, 0–3 months: 8 costumes that work lying down

Newborns sleep through most of the evening, so the costume must look right strapped into the car seat, or laid on a rug. Swaddle loosely at the hips: a 2026 survey of [436 mothers in Riyadh](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13465751), found knowledge of correct swaddling averaged 46.9%, and tight swaddling that holds the legs straight is a known hip-dysplasia risk.

- **Spring roll:** golden muslin wrapped loosely below the armpits. Safety: legs bent and free; unwrap after the photo. Est. US$0–5.
- **Sushi roll:** white swaddle, black felt band as nori, orange beanie as salmon. Safety: band stays below the armpits. Est. US$5.
- **Baby bat:** black sleepsuit, felt wings stitched wrist to side seam. Safety: no wire. Est. US$6–8.
- **Peanut:** tan sleepsuit with brown fabric-paint shell lines. Safety: wash the paint once before wearing. Est. US$5.
- **Glow-worm:** green sleepsuit, yellow felt tummy, beanie with felt antennae. Safety: no pipe cleaners. Est. US$6.
- **Dumpling:** cream sleepsuit, beanie with pleats sewn into the crown. Safety: beanie off indoors. Est. US$5.
- **Tiny mushroom:** white sleepsuit, red beanie with sewn white felt dots. Safety: never glued. Est. US$6.
- **Snoozing sloth:** brown sleepsuit, felt sloth face on the chest. Safety: no hood over the face. Est. US$7.

### 3–6 months: 8 costumes for tummy time and supported sitting

From three to six months, babies do tummy time and start sitting with support. Keep decorations flat, because padding on the back or tummy tips them over.

- **Turtle:** green sleepsuit, flat felt hexagon shell sewn on the back. Safety: no stuffing. Est. US$7.
- **Bumblebee:** yellow sleepsuit, iron-on black stripes, small felt wings. Safety: palm-sized wings only. Est. US$7.
- **Strawberry:** red sleepsuit, stitched felt seeds, leaf beanie. Safety: no sequins. Est. US$7.
- **Frog:** green sleepsuit, felt eyes on a green beanie. Safety: eyes are felt circles, not plastic toy eyes. Est. US$6.
- **Gumball machine:** white bodysuit with painted dots, red leggings. Safety: paint the gumballs; pom-poms choke. Est. US$6.
- **Octopus:** purple sleepsuit, six short felt legs stitched flat at the hip. Safety: nothing loose. Est. US$9.
- **Hedgehog:** brown sleepsuit, zigzag felt strip sewn down the back. Safety: soft felt only. Est. US$7.
- **Watermelon slice:** pink top, green leggings, stitched felt seeds. Safety: two pieces ease nappy changes. Est. US$6.

### 6–9 months: 8 costumes for sitting and crawling

Sitters chew whatever they reach, and crawlers drag fabric under their knees. Nothing hangs past the hands or feet.

- **Scuba diver:** blue sleepsuit, flat felt air tank sewn on the back. Safety: no mask or snorkel. Est. US$7.
- **Dalmatian puppy:** white sleepsuit, black felt spots, ears on a beanie. Safety: spots stitched, not stuck. Est. US$7.
- **Tiny doctor:** green bodysuit, felt stethoscope sewn flat. Safety: no toy tubing. Est. US$6.
- **Crab:** red sleepsuit, felt claws sewn to the shoulders, not the hands. Safety: hands stay free. Est. US$7.
- **Fox:** orange sleepsuit, white chest patch, short tail. Safety: tail stitched flat. Est. US$8.
- **Pilot:** khaki sleepsuit, felt wings badge, soft aviator-style beanie. Safety: skip the goggles and chin strap. Est. US$8.
- **Skunk:** black sleepsuit with a white felt stripe from head to bottom. Safety: a palm-length tail, sewn down. Est. US$7.
- **Shark:** grey sleepsuit, soft felt fin on the back, white felt teeth on the tummy. Safety: teeth away from the face. Est. US$7.

### 9–12 months: 8 costumes for cruising

Cruisers pull up on furniture and side-step, so nothing goes below the ankle. Separates beat one-pieces now for quick changes.

- **Firefighter:** red top and trousers with yellow felt stripes. Safety: no helmet; a soft red beanie instead. Est. US$8.
- **Elephant:** grey top and leggings, felt ears on a beanie. Safety: trunk stays short and on the hat. Est. US$8.
- **Mountain hiker:** fleece top, felt map patch, knitted beanie. Safety: non-slip socks, not new shoes. Est. US$5.
- **Dinosaur:** green top with felt plates sewn into the back seam. Safety: tail ends above the knee. Est. US$9.
- **Zebra:** white top and leggings with black fabric-paint stripes. Safety: hems above the ankle. Est. US$6.
- **Raccoon:** grey top, ringed felt tail, black felt "mask" on the beanie. Safety: no face paint. Est. US$7.
- **Painter:** white dungarees with fabric-paint splashes, beret with no elastic. Safety: no brush prop. Est. US$6.
- **Pizza slice:** felt tabard ending at the hips, stitched pepperoni. Safety: open sides, no ties at the neck. Est. US$6.

## Baby Halloween costumes by stage: cost and safety compared

The table puts the four stages side by side, using one costume from each list. Costs are estimates for a home-made version on a sleepsuit you already own.

| Stage | Costume example | Safety note | Est. cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Newborn, 0–3 months | Spring roll | Loose at the hips; photo only | US$0–5 |
| 3–6 months | Turtle | Flat decorations for tummy time | US$7 |
| 6–9 months | Crab | Hands, knees and feet clear | US$7 |
| 9–12 months | Dinosaur | Nothing below the knee or ankle | US$9 |

The pattern is that cost barely moves, while the safety focus slides from the face down to the feet. A sleepsuit costume also goes back into everyday rotation on 1 November.

## Baby costume safety: what 3 US rules cover, and what they skip

US federal rules protect costumed babies less than parents assume. Under [16 CFR part 1501](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-II/subchapter-C/part-1501), any toy or article meant for under-3s that fits inside the official test cylinder is banned as a choking hazard. Yet section 1501.3 exempts children's clothing and accessories, naming buttons, so costume trims are not run through that test.

That leaves the pull test to you. Tug every pom-pom, button and felt eye; if it moves, resew it or cut it off.

Flame rules have a similar gap. [16 CFR part 1615](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-II/subchapter-D/part-1615) sets the flammability test for children's sleepwear sizes 0–6X, with part 1616 covering sizes 7–14. It exempts "infant garments" sized nine months or smaller, and a costume is not sleepwear at all, so keep candles and lit jack-o'-lanterns out of reach and change the baby into their usual sleepwear for bed.

Overheating is the next risk. When researchers tested [nine babies carried in a sling](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC7202982) in 2020, 15 minutes of babywearing raised skin temperature by up to 1.1°C on the abdomen, and the mothers noticed no change. Feel the baby's tummy or nape, not their fingers, to judge warmth.

Face paint is out for the whole first year. [WA Health advises](https://health.wa.gov.au/Articles/F_I/Face-and-body-painting) against painting the face of any child under 3, because paint can get into the eyes or mouth and young skin is more sensitive. Put the whiskers on the beanie instead.

## Sending the costume photo to grandparents in Family mode

Grandparents far away want this photo most. Our [Halloween greeting page with Family mode](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) holds six pictures, a letter and one word that glows on a carved pumpkin. In this mode the closing question reads "Will you be my favourite little pumpkin?"

Grandad raps on the haunted-house door three times, clears misted portraits one by one to uncover the baby, and, up in the dark attic, shines a light on your note. You hear by email when he first answers, and his Boo License downloads as an Instagram Story-sized image.

For a month-by-month set, the [premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) fits a dozen photos plus a recorded message lasting at most 60 seconds, enough for a giggle. Site-wide, 38.5% of creators on SubhSandesh set a password first, a habit worth copying when the pictures show your baby.

## When to skip the baby costume, or the card

Leave the costume in the drawer if the baby is unwell, overtired or pulls at hats; a plain sleepsuit still photographs well. Halloween falls in late spring in Australia, and van de Kamp and Daanen say the familiar "one extra layer" rule needs rethinking in heat, so a warm evening may call for a nappy and one felt badge.

Our Halloween page has its own limits. It speaks English only and each page greets a single person. A granny who never got a smartphone will treasure a printed photo instead, and twenty cousins suit a shared album better.

- 16 CFR part 1615, children's sleepwear flammability, sizes 0–6X, eCFR (as of 1 October 2026): [ecfr.gov](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-II/subchapter-D/part-1615)
- WA Health, Face and body painting, undated: [health.wa.gov.au](https://health.wa.gov.au/Articles/F_I/Face-and-body-painting)
- van de Kamp and Daanen, IJERPH (MDPI), 13 August 2025: [Europe PMC](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12386404)
- Filingeri et al., Physiological Reports, 6 May 2020: [Europe PMC](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC7202982)
